title: Her secrets: old featherfans, tasselled dancecards, powdered with musk, a gaud of amber beads in her locked drawer. A birdcage hung in the sunny window of her house when she was a girl.
html_source:
Stephen is remembering his mother as a young girl, long before he was born, with her stereotypical fascinations common with little girls.
Her past is a secret she has left behind now.

This perspective induces him to imagine her life without him, before the insurmountable task of motherhood, one which inevitably makes a person accountable for another human being, was bestowed upon her. Stephen is most probably using anecdotes to get a more vivid picture of his mother in her independent days, something more tangible to relate to without prejudiced compassion.
